title: Extension of scalars is right exact
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], the functor $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$
preserves finite colimits.

proof.text: Under precisely the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] gives the natural adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ between $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and $\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$. Thus the extension functor in the statement is a left adjoint.

source.place: Proof, first clause; unit sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, part 2

proof.text: Let $I$ be any finite category, and let $M:I\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ have a colimit cocone $(L,(\iota_i)_i)$. Finite categories are small, so apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the adjunction of step 1, with its $L$ equal to $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ and its $R$ equal to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. It states that $(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi L,(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\iota_i)_i)$ is a colimit cocone of $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\circ M$. Since finite colimits are exactly the colimits indexed by finite categories [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], this is preservation of finite colimits. Only preservation of existing colimits is asserted; existence of all finite colimits in the source is not required.
